blind_spots.blind_spot: Contributor-intelligence products need live upstream network access; the cyber defenders named in their own contract do not have it
blind_spots.operator_reality: DepsDiver's whole value is knowing who maintains a package — that means continuously reaching npm/PyPI/GitHub and their contributor graph. A defender working an SDA/PWSA program does that work inside an air-gapped or IL5 enclave where the IDE has no route to a vendor cloud and package registries are mirrored, stale, and stripped of contributor metadata. The tool that lights up on a commercial laptop returns nothing on the network where the contract lives — the same class of failure as the 30fps crowd-detection case, where the architecture assumed connectivity the environment denies.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The product was clearly designed commercial-first (IDE extension, CLI, free trial, self-serve pricing) and the SDA award arrived at launch, before anyone had to run it inside a real enclave.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Enhance your coding workflow with our VSIX extension for VS Code and other supported editors (Cursor, Windsurf, etc.).

blind_spots.blind_spot: No visible path through the DoD software factory that would actually host this tool
blind_spots.operator_reality: A scanner that enforces policy 'across the software lifecycle' has to live in the customer's CI/CD — which in DoD means Platform One / Iron Bank, a hardened container image, STIG compliance, and a signed authorization package before it runs on a single pipeline. That accreditation work is measured in months and is the single line item most likely to outrun the funded period of performance on a Phase II. Nothing in their material names Iron Bank, container hardening, a Phase III sole-source path, or a government sponsor who would carry the ATO.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Founders came from threat research and intelligence, where the deliverable is a report; the artifact that gets software fielded is an authorization package, and that is a different discipline than the one that won the award.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Ongoing security monitoring and enforcement designed to prevent adversarial foreign ownership, control, and influence across the software lifecycle.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Scanning DoD codebases means ingesting CUI at a 10-person pre-seed with no stated compliance posture
blind_spots.operator_reality: The dependency manifests and SBOMs of a space-vehicle program are not neutral metadata — they describe the composition of a defense system and are handled as CUI, with NIST 800-171/CMMC obligations on the vendor holding them. Their own research already advertises visibility into 'container images in Node.js and Department of Defense systems'. If that data is transiting a commercial SaaS backend without a documented CMMC posture, the contract can die on a compliance finding rather than on the technology.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Pre-seed companies defer CMMC until a contracting officer forces the issue, and with no compliance or security-program hire visible, no one internally owns it.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Solo maintainer poses supply chain risk to more than 5,000 software packages, including container images in Node.js and Department of Defense systems

opener_hook: Hunted Labs' Space Development Agency Phase II (FA254125CB028) is scoped to harden software for DoD cyber defenders, but DepsDiver's contributor intelligence depends on live registry access — which the enclaves those defenders work in do not have.
what_they_do: Software supply-chain security tooling (DepsDiver, Entercept) that identifies foreign adversarial ownership and influence behind the open-source packages a codebase depends on.
